title: Béisbol o fútbol
desc: An argument nobody wants to win
setting: Four young men from the workshop, one bench, and don Emilio sitting behind not saying anything.

steps.speaker: Muchacho
steps.es: El béisbol ya pasó de moda. Eso es de viejos.
steps.en: Baseball is out of fashion. That is for old people.

options.es: Ah, de viejos. Decile eso a don Emilio, ahí está.
options.en: Ah, for old people. Say that to don Emilio, he is right there.
options.feedback: You hooked his own word and turned it round in one line. That is how you enter without pushing.

options.es: No es cierto, mucha gente juega.
options.en: That is not true, lots of people play.
options.feedback: A flat contradiction. It answers with facts, which is where this argument goes to die.
Numbers end the night. Nobody at that bench came for numbers.

steps.speaker: Muchacho
steps.es: Es que en el mundo entero se ve fútbol.
steps.en: The thing is the whole world watches football.

options.es: En el mundo entero, sí. Aquí no, aquí es otra cosa.
options.en: In the whole world, yes. Not here, here it is another thing.
options.feedback: You conceded the big half and kept the half that matters. Very hard to argue with.
Agreement, which is the same as leaving the bench.
A verdict where a story was called for. Now it is opinions against opinions.

steps.speaker: Muchacho
steps.es: ¿Y vos qué sabés? Si no sos de aquí.
steps.en: And what do you know? You are not even from here.

options.es: Fui al estadio con Marcos hace cuatro años. Contame vos.
options.en: I went to the stadium with Marcos four years ago. You tell me.
options.feedback: A memory beats a credential. It also invites him to keep going instead of shutting him down.

options.en: I have been here five years.
options.feedback: True, and it argues about your right to be in the conversation rather than about baseball.
Now the argument is about the two of you, which is the one thing it was never about.

steps.speaker: Don Emilio
steps.es: (al pasar, le pone la mano en el hombro) Buen juego el domingo.
steps.en: (passing, he puts a hand on your shoulder) A good game on Sunday.

options.en: I will be there, don Emilio.
options.feedback: He ended the argument with a hand and a half-sentence. You answered the half-sentence and left the hand alone.
Warm. It is also a shade louder than the gesture.

options.en: I am right, am I not, don Emilio?
options.feedback: Recruiting him into the argument after he had ended it with one hand.
